reason: I'll start with the biceps: the front of the arm has a space for it, and muscle cells seem like the pieces to fill it.
expectation: I expect the muscle cells to form the biceps in the front of the arm, though I'm not sure exactly how they'll be assembled.

alternatives.reason: I could strengthen the front bone first, but I want to build the muscle first.

effect: The muscle cells formed a biceps connected to the tendons, but the front bone still needs mineral.
reaction: It was useful to see the separate cells join into long fibres.
reason: I'll add mineral to the front bone to finish the biceps attachment goal.
expectation: I expect the mineral to strengthen the radius at the attachment, though I'm not sure what the completed model will show.

alternatives.reason: I could start the triceps now, but I'd rather finish the front first.

effect: The front is complete, and the demonstration shows the biceps pulling the radius to bend the elbow. The back still needs muscle and mineral.
reaction: Seeing the muscle pull the bone made the elbow movement clearer.
reason: I'll build the triceps next, using muscle cells in the back of the arm.
expectation: I expect the cells to form the triceps between its tendons, like they formed the biceps.

alternatives.reason: I could mineralize the back bone first, but I want to see the triceps built.

effect: The triceps is in place, but the ulna still needs mineral before the back is complete.
reaction: The triceps formed much like the biceps, which was predictable.
reason: I'll add mineral to the back bone; it's the only available combination and should complete the triceps attachment.
expectation: I expect the ulna to become stronger and the model to show how the triceps straightens the elbow.

effect: The back is complete, and the demonstration shows how the triceps pulls behind the elbow to straighten it.
reaction: The comparison with the biceps made it clearer how attachment changes the direction of movement.

mostWorthwhile.text: Completing the front was most worthwhile because the demonstration connected the biceps pulling to the elbow bending.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps felt somewhat repetitive after building the biceps, although its different position mattered later.

surprise.text: The same kind of pulling cells can produce opposite elbow movements depending on where the muscles attach.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary: the named slots and goals explained the pairings, though the menu also confirmed they were compatible.

continue.text: I'd probably continue: seeing the completed arm demonstrate how muscle and bone work together made me curious about other body systems.
